newsitem.title: FRANCE: French prosecutor urges jail for Dev Sol Turks.
newsitem.headline: French prosecutor urges jail for Dev Sol Turks.

text.p: A state prosecutor asked a Paris court on Thursday to jail 11 suspected members of the far left Turkish guerrilla movement Dev Sol on terrorism charges.
Anti-terrorist prosecutor Anne Obez-Vosgien requested at least six years in prison for the main suspect, Dursun Karatas, a founder of the far-left group who is being tried in absentia.
Arrested during a routine border check in 1994, Karatas fled France after being released on bail the following year.
Obez-Vosgien asked the court to jail for three years German journalist Ursula Hoppe-Unlu, who was described in court as a former member of the German leftist guerrilla movement the Red Army Faction.
A French communist-controlled journalists' union protested against her being put on trial, saying "her only crime was to have recorded the Turkish state's repression of democrats and Kurds".

The prosecutor requested sentences ranging from two to five years against the nine other defendants, eight of whom were in court. All 11 were on trial for belonging to an illegal group engaged in terrorist activities.
French authorities accuse Dev Sol guerrillas of damaging Turkish property in Paris, Strasbourg and Lyon between 1981 and 1992 and extorting money from Turkish businesses.
But investigators were unable to pin specific attacks on any of the defendants who were also prosecuted for using forged identity papers and entering France illegally.
Dev Sol, created in 1978, is held responsible for the deaths of several hundred people in Turkey, including the murder of then justice minister Mehmet Topac in 1994.
